title: Aptitude Tests and Neuropsychological Tests
summary: Aptitude testing (GATB, ASVAB, Guilford-Zimmerman); neuropsychological testing (Clock Drawing, Halstead-Reitan, Luria-Nebraska, MMSE, Bender-Gestalt, WCST); clinical applications.
objectives: Define aptitude test and give examples.
Describe major neuropsychological tests and domains.
revision: Aptitude tests measure potential (GATB, ASVAB, Guilford-Zimmerman). Neuropsychological tests assess brain-behaviour function (Clock Drawing, Halstead-Reitan, Luria-Nebraska, MMSE, Bender-Gestalt, WCST).

notes.t: A test that measures a person's potential to learn or acquire a specific skill with training.
Aptitude tests guide vocational counselling and personnel selection. Neuropsychological tests assist in diagnosing brain injury, dementia and neurological disorders.
UGC NET frequently asks to match neuropsychological tests with their assessed domains (e.g., WCST = set-shifting, MMSE = cognitive screening).
